activity_context.topic_title: Applying the Integration By Parts Twice

feedback.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}(x)-\int (x)(\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-2\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x))(x)-\int (x)(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)-\int \text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)-x+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is a constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =x{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-2(x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)-x+D) \\  & =x{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+2x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-2D.$ 

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & ={(x{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+2x)|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =(e{(\operatorname{ln}⁡e)}^{2}-2e\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)+2e)-(1{(\operatorname{ln}⁡1)}^{2}-2\cdot 1\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)+2(1)) \\  & =e-2.\end{aligned}
$$
